design_rationale:
WORKLOG — equipment_rental_desk, task 1. "Staying on: five more days on the hire skis."

STEP 0 — DRAW, SNAPSHOT AND CLAIM.
Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/equipment_rental_desk --tasks 2):
  {"task": 1, "key": "ski_resort_operator/equipment_rental_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 5]}
So this task is a tree of three problems, and the three factor counts are assigned: 4 to the change
of model fee, 5 to the hire rate, and 6 to the extension charge. The tree and the factor sets were
chosen after the draw was read, never the other way round.

Already occupied by task 0: rentals_ext_damage_assessment, rentals_ext_late_handin_fee,
rentals_ext_counter_settlement and rentals_ext_security_hold_settlement, with their four tools, all
of them on the settling-up side of the charter — what a technician found, what days beyond the date
on the agreement cost, what the guest hands over and what goes back from the security hold. Claimed
here: rentals_ext_model_change_fee, rentals_ext_party_rate_charge and rentals_ext_extension_charge,
with three new tools, all of them on the live-hire side — changing the kit, pricing the hire and
running it on. The two scopes share no policy, no tool and no computed parameter. Nothing is left
for a later task: with these three the difficulty's seven extended policies are covered and the two
tasks' scopes are disjoint and complete.

DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: a guest on a week's skiing wants to keep his hire skis five days longer
and has already put the request in through the collective's app. Scored core parameter: what keeping
them costs. The chain the policy forces: the charge for the extra days is fixed only after the hire
rate for the days the agreement was written for stands on its rental account, because each extra day
is charged at the rate the agreement was actually written on; and it is fixed only after every change
of model recorded on the agreement carries the shop's fee owed for it, because a hire that has
already paid for counter work is not charged the extension fee again. Neither stands on the account
at the opening: the package takes its money at collection, the kit was collected on the fourteenth,
and yet the only charge on the account is the helmet add-on; and the agreement records a change of
model, confirmed by the shop's own size change request, with no fee entry anywhere. Depth is two hops
from the goal to each prerequisite; breadth is three products read in parallel (passes, lessons,
lodging), two shop requests, and four stretches of the rental ledger.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller gives one date and nothing else that matters. The number has to
be assembled from: which of three day-rate rules the agreement's length selects; which of three
day-count rules its state selects; nine lift scans inside a three-month window and two more just
outside it; a school booking and a lodging reservation that both bear on the bundle share, of which
only the larger is ever taken; thirteen days of advance lead; a departure date that falls exactly on
the date the kit is asked to be kept to; two days of notice measured back from the due date; a helmet
charged as its own entry and carried on into the extra days; and the two entries the desk itself has
to put on the account first. An agent who prices the extension straight off the package's rate card
gets a confident 205.00 instead of 87.73 and never sees a signal.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- Write at action 11 (subjects rentals_swap and rentals_fee_charge). Governing base policies:
  rentals_swap_and_extension and rentals_late_return.
  rentals_swap_and_extension has no structured gate, so the write carries the policy's scope: changes
  are counted on the agreement and a rider who has used the package's allowance is offered a new
  agreement rather than a further change. The Basic package allows one change and the agreement
  records one, so the allowance is not exceeded.
  rentals_late_return gate fee_bearing_agreement_state: "A fee is raised against an agreement only
  while the agreement stands in the confirmed, picked_up, overdue, returned, cancelled or no_show
  state." Authority system_record, pre-action, correlation key rentals_holdings.rental_id bound to
  the call's rental_id. The agreement stands picked_up, inside the allowed set. The policy's other
  gate, grace_has_run_out, applies to rentals_mark_overdue and is not realized by this write.
- Write at action 13 (subject rentals_rate_charge). Governing base policies: rentals_agg_party_pricing
  and rentals_pricing.
  rentals_agg_party_pricing has no structured gate; its scope is the passholder and bundle reductions
  and the rule that only the largest bundle reduction is taken, never both added together.
  rentals_pricing gate chargeable_agreement_state: "A charge is raised against an agreement only
  while the agreement stands in the reserved, confirmed, picked_up or overdue state." The agreement
  stands picked_up, inside the allowed set.
- Write at action 15 (subjects rentals_extend and rentals_fee_charge). Governing base policies:
  rentals_swap_and_extension and rentals_late_return, the same two gates as at action 11.
  rentals_swap_and_extension's scope also carries the two boundaries this write must respect: the
  package must allow extension at all and the extension may not exceed the package's limit, and an
  extension is recorded before the kit falls due rather than after. The Basic package allows
  extension by up to seven days; five are asked for; the kit is due back on 2027-02-18 and the
  handling date is 2027-02-17, so the kit has not fallen due. Positive and negative boundary cases:
  had the handling date been 2027-02-19 with the kit still out, the agreement would stand overdue and
  the extension route would be closed, the correct handling being a late hand-in instead; and had the
  guest asked for the kit to 2027-02-26, eight days, the request would exceed the package's limit and
  only seven could be taken.
  No time eligibility gate is realized by any of the three writes, so temporal_feasibility is [].

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target object: the one rental agreement on the household account, the Basic Ski
& Board Rental hired at Hollow Creek, collected 2027-02-14 and written down to come back 2027-02-18.
Correlation key: rentals_holdings.rental_id, carried by every ledger entry and both shop requests.
Rows that enter the sums: the block of five days loaded, the three dates the kit has been out, the
helmet add-on of 60.00 and the security hold of 150.00; and, once this conversation has written them,
the change-of-model fee and the hire rate. Rows deliberately excluded by a visible key: the two lift
scans of 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-31, outside the three-month window; the school tuition charge, which
is not a session delivered; the date the kit was out on serial BSKI4102MT, which is the serial the
rider collected rather than the one the agreement now shows, and which is why the change of model on
the agreement is a fact and not an inference. Settlements already made: none — no payment entry
stands on this agreement at all, which is exactly why the outstanding figure equals the helmet add-on
to the cent. Both writes the desk makes carry the agreement's own reference.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root: rentals_ext_extension_charge (extension_charge_usd, owner USER — the guest confirms a charge
  on his own hire himself, and the agent unlocks the confirmation and hands it across).
  edge 1: rentals_ext_extension_charge <- rentals_ext_party_rate_charge.
    kind value_input, gate rate_charged, form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "The charge for the extra days is fixed only after the hire rate for the
    days the agreement was written for stands on its rental account."
    Four-point test: (1) "only after" joins this policy's own result to what it waits on; (2) the XX
    side is a record-visible state — a hire rate entry standing on the rental account — naming no
    action and no performer; (3) no tool, no policy id, no snake_case token; (4) a hard requirement,
    scoped exactly to the hire rate for the days the agreement was written for. Exactly one write of
    this difficulty brings that state about: the party rate charge policy's own action is the only
    one in the charter that puts a hire rate on a rental account. Derivation: the sentence says the
    extension charge waits on the hire rate standing; the records show six entries, none of them a
    hire rate, and an outstanding figure equal to the helmet add-on alone; the party rate charge
    policy's rule says how an agreement's hire rate is built and that it is put on the account;
    therefore the rate must be raised first, and no other reading is available.
    Seed evidence it does not hold at the opening: the account's only charge entry carries the helmet
    add-on category, and the agreement's outstanding figure stands at 60.00.
    Resolving action: the hire rate action, owner agent.
  edge 2: rentals_ext_extension_charge <- rentals_ext_model_change_fee.
    kind value_input, gate change_fee_entries, form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "The charge for the extra days is fixed only after every change of model
    recorded on the agreement carries the shop's fee owed for it."
    Four-point test: (1) "only after"; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — a change recorded
    on the agreement carrying a fee entry — with no action named; (3) no code names; (4) hard, and
    scoped exactly to changes of model recorded on this agreement. Exactly one write of this
    difficulty books that entry: the model change fee policy's own action. Derivation: the sentence
    says the extension charge waits on every recorded change carrying its fee; the records show a
    change count of one and a confirmed size change request, and no entry of the shop fee family;
    the model change fee policy's rule says what such a fee is and how it is worked out; therefore
    that fee must be raised first.
    Seed evidence: the agreement's change count of 1 and the size change request standing confirmed,
    against a rental account whose six entries are the block loaded, three dates out, the helmet
    add-on and the security hold.
    Resolving action: the change-of-model fee action, owner agent.
  topological order: the change fee, the hire rate, the extension. The first two are parallel;
  order_uniqueness in the task file gives the replayed proof that they commute.
  value_input edges: 2, against the floor of max(2-1, 1) = 1.
  Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skipping the hire rate moves the extension charge from
  87.73 to 120.24; skipping the change fee moves it from 87.73 to 97.73.
  Nothing in the tree waits on anything outside this conversation: both prerequisites are book
  entries the desk makes on the spot, and the confirmation is a button the guest presses while he is
  on the line. No status write stands in for a real-world event.

FACTOR CARD (figures from the Step 5 sensitivity run; per-factor detail sits in each computation's
factor_trace).
  rentals_ext_model_change_fee (4 factors, 3 parameter + 1 method): change_window_basis (method) ->
    9.75; change_timing_share -> 9.75; instruction_referral_share (lessons) -> 11.70;
    kit_value_uplift_level -> 4.50. Whole baseline 15.00 against gold 5.85.
  rentals_ext_party_rate_charge (5 factors, 3 parameter + 2 method): day_rate_basis (method) ->
    141.24; chargeable_day_basis (method) -> 71.85; passholder_share_level (passes, multi-source) ->
    140.89; bundle_share_level (lessons, multi-source) -> 140.89; advance_share_level (multi-source)
    -> 140.89. Whole baseline 138.00 against gold 119.76.
  rentals_ext_extension_charge (6 factors, 5 parameter + 1 method): extra_day_rate_basis (method) ->
    120.24; free_extension_days (passes, multi-source) -> 146.22; residence_share_level (lodging) ->
    100.66; notice_share_level -> 93.48; helmet_carry_on (multi-source) -> 51.73;
    extension_fee_level (multi-source) -> 97.73. Whole baseline 205.00 against gold 87.73.
  Multi-source factors of the task: passholder_share_level, bundle_share_level, advance_share_level,
  kit_value_uplift_level, free_extension_days, helmet_carry_on, extension_fee_level.
  Cross-difficulty factors: instruction_referral_share (lessons), passholder_share_level (passes),
  bundle_share_level (lessons), free_extension_days (passes), residence_share_level (lodging).
  No factor's tier is read off a stamp: each rests on counted or summed ledger rows, a date span, or
  another product's holding and ledger.
  Near misses planted on purpose: the two lift scans of late October, on the same pass but outside
  the three-month window; the school tuition entry, which is an entry but not a session delivered;
  the date the kit was out on the serial the rider collected rather than the serial the agreement now
  shows; and a lodging departure date that falls exactly on the date the kit is asked to be kept to,
  where "on or after" and "after" give different tiers.
  Inherited base boundaries this task does not touch: the fitting range, the term bounds, the hold
  placement and release rules, the fee-bearing state. The base clauses superseded are declared in
  four overwrite entries — the blanket free first refit, the per-rider passholder reduction, the flat
  advance booking reduction, the extra days at the rate the agreement was written on together with
  the extension fee on top, and add-ons only ever raised as their own entries — each naming the base
  sentence it replaces and the extended sentence that takes its place.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
  customers: the household the call is about; without it nothing can be located or verified.
  rentals_holdings: the agreement every computation reads — the dates the length, the advance lead
    and the notice are measured on, the state that picks the day-count rule and the helmet tier, the
    package that supplies every tier parameter, the change count and the days written for that the
    extra-day figure is divided by.
  rentals_ledger block load: the five days the agreement was written for, against which the three
    drawn leave two remaining.
  rentals_ledger three dates out: the change window, the days the hire rate is charged for, and the
    serial evidence for the change of model. Remove them and both method factors fall to other tiers.
  rentals_ledger helmet add-on: the helmet carry-on factor, and the reason the outstanding figure is
    60.00 rather than nothing.
  rentals_ledger security hold: the uplift on the change fee.
  rentals_requests size change: the date the change was raised, which the change window falls back on
    when no date the kit was out is recorded.
  rentals_requests extension: the date the kit is asked to be kept to and the date the notice was
    given — the extra days and the notice share both rest on it, and it is where the write's date
    parameter is read from.
  passes_holdings and passes_ledger: the passholder share on the rate and the free days on the
    extension.
  lodging_holdings: the bundle share on the rate and the residence share on the extension.
  lessons_holdings and lessons_ledger: the instruction share on the change fee and the bundle share
    on the rate.
  Automatic-clause check: the base charter's automatic clauses here are the reservation hold period
  running out into an uncollected reservation, the grace period running out into an overdue flag, and
  closure once nothing is left to collect. None is lit: the kit was collected, so no uncollected
  reservation can arise; the kit is not yet due, so no overdue flag is owed; and the agreement still
  owes money at the end, so closure is not owed either. No cache trap is used: the agreement's
  remaining days and outstanding figure both agree exactly with the ledger at the opening.

PERSONA DESIGN. Casimir Nwachukwu-Hale is written as a man ringing from a ski week rather than from a
desk: he leads with the thing he wants, mentions the app request because it is how he came to ring,
and then waits. That keeps the surface goal to one sentence and one date. His identity details come
out one at a time and only when asked. His authorisation is split and explicit — the desk may do
whatever the shop has to do at its end, but he wants to press the confirmation himself, which is
exactly the hand-over the tree needs and the reason the root problem is his own write. What he can
answer about the week is the natural circumstance a guest remembers: the collection date, the
lessons, the room running to the twenty-third. He offers no figure, does not ask for one before he is
told, and does not dispute the one he is given, so he can never pull a wrong agent back onto the
path. He closes on hearing the skis are booked through and what it comes to, which is exactly where
the last gold action leaves the call.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. He gives a name and a mobile, which locate the account; a date of
birth, which completes verification. The agent reads the agreement, the rental account, the shop
requests, the pass and its scans, the lodging reservation, the school booking and its sessions — all
share tools, all synchronous. The change-of-model fee and the hire rate are book entries. The
confirmation is a button the agent unlocks and hands across and the guest presses while he is on the
line. Every must-ask question has an answer in the persona, and the whole tree runs under one
frozen_time with no waiting, no clearing and no future date.

WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT.
  Pricing the extra days off the package's rate card at 39.00 a day instead of at the rate the
  agreement was actually written on, 23.95 — the rule's tiers turn on whether the hire rate stands on
  the account, which is why it has to be raised first.
  Charging all five extra days instead of three, by missing the two days the pass and its scans give
  free.
  Charging the package's extension fee of 10.00 on top, when the account carries a change-of-model
  fee and the agreement runs at or above the multi-day threshold.
  Forgetting the helmet, which is charged as its own entry for the original days and carried into the
  extra ones at 12.00 a day.
  Taking the lodging departure date of 2027-02-23 as falling before the date the kit is asked to be
  kept to, when it falls on it, and so taking the post-stay share instead of the resident share.
  Adding the lesson and lodging bundle shares together on the hire rate instead of taking only the
  larger.
  Counting the two October scans inside the three-month window, or the tuition entry as a session
  delivered.
  Charging the hire rate for the three dates the kit has been out instead of for the length of the
  agreement, or at the shop day rate instead of the multi-day rate.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify. Read the agreement, the rental account, the shop requests, the
pass, the pass entries, the lodging reservation, the school booking and the school entries. Work out
the change-of-model fee: window of three dates out less one is two days, inside the fitting window of
three, so 60 percent of 15.00; the school delivered two sessions in the month, so 50 percent; the
hold of 150.00 and five days booked give a 30 percent uplift; 15.00 x 0.60 x 0.50 x 1.30 = 5.85.
Raise it. Work out the hire rate: five days at the multi-day rate of 39.00 = 195.00; less 15 percent
passholder = 165.75; less the larger bundle share of 15 percent = 140.89; less 15 percent advance =
119.76. Raise it. Work out the extension: five extra days capped at seven, less two free = three;
each at 119.76 over five days = 23.95, taken at 80 percent resident and 90 percent early notice, plus
12.00 a day for the helmet; no extension fee; 3 x (23.95 x 0.8 x 0.9 + 12.00) = 87.73. Unlock the
confirmation, hand it to the guest, and he books the kit through to 2027-02-23.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The three computations were evaluated by the gate's own machinery on the
handling-time world (initial_state plus every earlier gold write), problem by problem in topological
order, and the per-factor baseline substitutions and the whole-baseline substitution were replayed on
the same worlds. Command and output:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/equipment_rental_desk --task 1
  rentals_ext_model_change_fee = 5.85 ; rentals_ext_party_rate_charge = 119.76 ;
  rentals_ext_extension_charge = 87.73
  per-factor baselines: 9.75 / 9.75 / 11.70 / 4.50 ; 141.24 / 71.85 / 140.89 / 140.89 / 140.89 ;
  120.24 / 146.22 / 100.66 / 93.48 / 51.73 / 97.73
  whole baselines: 15.00 / 138.00 / 205.00, each different from its gold.
Every figure equals the corresponding computations entry and the gold argument at its step.

FORWARD AND REVERSE SWEEP. Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice quotes the
rule sentence it implements in compute_basis — the aggregations, the cross-category reads, every
ladder and the rounding. Reverse: each rule read through, every sentence carrying a quantity, a
window, a filter, a branch, an order or a rounding is claimed by a binding. The windows ("in the
month before the change is priced", "in the three months before") correspond to within_months on the
matching aggregate; the filters ("the shop's fee for a change of model", "the package's helmet
add-on", "the hire rate") correspond to the event_type and charge_category filters; the branch words
("where ... instead") correspond to ternaries; the limits ("never more than the package's extension
limit") correspond to MN; the rounding words correspond to RND. Each rule states its acting base, its
order and its rounding moment in plain prose: on the change fee the three act on the package's change
fee itself rather than on one another's results; on the hire rate the passholder share acts on the
days at the day rate, the bundle share on what that left and the advance share on what the bundle
step left, with a rounding at the end of each; on the extension the resident and notice shares act on
the daily figure itself, the helmet addition is added after both, and the extension fee is added once
to the whole rather than to each day.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. Each of the three calls carries its business effect, its request
binding with an intent source and a discriminator, its stage provenance and its base preconditions.
The two prerequisites are state_due and cite the records that owe them; the root is on_request and
cites the caller's own words, with the discriminator's business phrase occurring verbatim in the
cited line. Stage provenance is honest: the change of model pre-exists the call and cites the
agreement's change count and the shop's confirmed request; the hire rate is performed by its own
tool; the extension is established by prior steps and cites them.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and
this worklog masked, and working only from the policy prose the knowledge base will carry, the three
tool schemas, the rows the share tools return and the caller's own lines: the caller asks to keep the
kit to the twenty-third; the extension rule says the charge rests on the extra days and the daily
figure, and states that it waits on the hire rate standing on the account and on every recorded
change carrying its fee; the account shows neither, so both must come first; the change fee rule and
the hire rate rule each yield one number on the records as they stand; the extension rule then yields
one number on the records the two writes leave. Working through gives 5.85, 119.76 and 87.73 and the
order change fee, hire rate, extension — the same conclusion, objects, parameters and order as gold,
with no second reading, since every tier condition is settled by a record rather than by judgement.

  check_extended.py --task 1    -> EXTENDED OK
  check_task_tools.py --task 1  -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (3 tools)

                                   closure 27 of 27 seeded rows)
  check_solvability.py --task 1 -> SOLVABILITY OK (3 calls, 6 base gates, 7 seed rows)
  check_compute.py --task 1     -> COMPUTE OK (3 computations, 15 factors, 5 cross-difficulty,

  check_cross_fire.py --task 1  -> SCOPE OK

REVISION RECORD. Symptom: the first run of check_extended and check_compute on this task reported
"only 0 multi-source factors over this task's policies". Root cause: several ladders had been written
with the second tier's test as a bare predicate ("otherwise, if the pass is active") rather than as
the full compound condition the ladder states in words, so the machine could see only one of the two
forks as a combination of distinct evidence. Change: each of those second tiers now tests, in compute,
exactly the compound condition its ladder states — the pass active and the scan count below the
threshold, the lodging held and no school booking, the lead long enough and the agreement below the
multi-day threshold, the fee entry present and the agreement below that threshold, the add-on present
and the kit not out, the hold high and the agreement below the threshold. Re-run: EXTENDED OK and
COMPUTE OK, with the figures unchanged at 5.85, 119.76 and 87.73, since this world sits on the first
tier of each of those ladders. A second symptom in the same run: check_solvability reported that a
state_due policy at step 15 "must cite a pre-action object-level system obligation, not caller
intent". Root cause: the extension charge had been declared state_due although it is a quote the
guest asks for and confirms, not a debt the month-end books would already owe. Change: its trigger is
now on_request, which is what it is, and its intent source is the caller's own line. Re-run:
SOLVABILITY OK. Both changes were propagated in the same pass to the rule text, the ladders, the
factor blocks and this worklog.

MANUAL VALUES GATES.
  Length, breadth and the hidden test: walked above from the caller's date to the extension charge,
  and from that charge back to the hire rate and to the change-of-model fee. Removing either edge
  changes the scored figure (87.73 -> 120.24 and 87.73 -> 97.73). The root problem is the guest's own
  write: agreeing to a charge on his own hire is his to do, the agent unlocks the confirmation and
  hands it across, and he presses it while he is on the line, so the in-person semantics are genuine
  and the act completes synchronously.
  Need and simulator boundary: he names the object (his hire skis), the timing (now, before they fall
  due), the new date, the authorisation split (the desk may do the shop's side; he presses the
  confirmation) and that he wants it done rather than quoted. He never reads policy, never pushes the
  procedure along, never corrects a figure and never leaks an answer.
  Chronology of the opening world: every fact he volunteers - the app request, the collection date,
  the lessons, the room running to the twenty-third - points at a seeded row, and none of them
  anticipates the change fee, the hire rate or the extension charge.
  Base eligibility and boundaries: aligned per subject above, with the package's extension limit and
  the before-it-falls-due rule checked in both directions; no time eligibility gate is realized, so
  temporal_feasibility is empty by construction rather than by omission.
  Authoritative facts and the business object: the change of model, the state of the hire and what
  has been charged all rest on records; the caller is never the authority for any of them.
  Reachability and no real-world waits: walked turn by turn above; nothing waits on a workshop, a
  clearing, a review or a future date.
  Prerequisite sentences: the four-point test is applied to both above; the state form carries both,
  so no fallback_reason arises, and each state is brought about by exactly one write of this
  difficulty.
  Two-way equivalence of rule and compute: swept in both directions above.
  Factors bear weight and the labels are honest: each of the fifteen moves its result; every
  computation clears the two-parameter and one-method floors; the four method factors change how a
  quantity is worked out - the window the change is measured in, the day rate the days are charged
  at, the days that are charged for, and the figure an extra day is charged at - rather than merely
  swapping a number; and no two tiers of any ladder select the same outcome.
  Draft recomputation from the visible context: recorded above; it reaches gold with no second
  reading.

================================================================================
REWORK ROUND 2 — answering the source-layer policy-task audit.
================================================================================
This task passed the audit on all four relationships, and its derivation agreed with every scored
value (5.85, 119.76, 87.73), the write order, the tree and every tier taken. One charter-global
finding was recorded as bearing on this task, and it is closed here; nothing else of this task was
touched, and no figure of it moved.

F-3 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, charter-global; T1-1 recorded that it does not bite this world) — the
  lesson-bundle-alone branch. Base rentals_agg_party_pricing states "The lesson bundle reduction is
  taken where the same rider also holds a snowsports school booking over the same dates, and the
  lodging bundle reduction where the household holds collective lodging over the same dates", and
  rentals_ext_party_rate_charge produced nothing for a rider who holds a school booking and no
  lodging, with no overwrite naming the dropped branch. Rather than declare base's sentence
